page.title: Approvals
page.purpose: Let the minter decide pending redemptions quickly, with enough context to decide well and a recorded reason when they decline.

priorities.statement: What is being asked for, by whom, and at what cost is readable without opening anything.
Approving and denying are equally reachable; neither is the visually default choice.
priorities.notes: A queue that makes approval the easy path stops being a decision surface.

priorities.statement: A denial captures a reason, because a refusal the holder cannot understand teaches nothing.
A request already decided elsewhere is shown as decided rather than silently overwritten.

states.description: One or more redemptions await a decision.
Nothing is waiting; the state is calm rather than celebratory.
Decision recorded and the queue updated.
A listed request was decided in another session; the row reports that instead of accepting a second decision.
Queue loaded but per-request holder context failed; rows render with context marked unavailable rather than hiding the request.

elements.name: Pending redemptions
elements.description: Each request with holder, entry, cost and age.

elements.name: Deny
elements.description: Releases the reservation and records a reason.

elements.name: Reason
elements.description: Why the request was denied, shown to the holder.

elements.name: Request context
elements.description: The holder's balance and recent activity, for deciding in context.

claims.statement: Approve and deny are equally prominent and equally reachable; neither is styled as the default.
Enough holder context to decide is present without leaving the queue.
Denying requires a reason before the decision can be submitted.
A row whose request was decided elsewhere is visually distinct and does not accept a second decision.
The empty queue reads as an ordinary state, not an achievement.
Every decision in the queue is operable by keyboard alone.
